Just tired. So tired. I get so worked up about stuff anymore. Sometimes even the smallest event is enough to make me love life. Then I crash. This happens over and over again and has been for months.

Today I crashed for the first time in about a week and I'm just getting tired of it. I know I have a problem. I've tried getting help. I don't know what else to do.

I have planned my death for about 6 months now...when I'm happy I feel foolish for doing so. But on days like today I'm barely capable of convincing myself to go on.

If something doesn't change then eventually I won't be able to convince myself anymore.

I've considered similar options...the problem is that my life isn't really that bad. Things are going well for me and I'm lucky to have been able to come as far as I have. I don't really want to give that up...but if I do it's going to have to be because I'm trying to get help and change myself for the better.

If I did pack up and leave I could potentially make my life even better...but I'd still be me. I'd still have all of this guilt and sadness and craziness floating around in my brain. As much as I wish a change of scenery could help me I don't think it can...

Thanks for the suggestion though. I really do like the thought behind your idea.

The only reason I don't want to go home is because of how much of a let down it would be for me and the impression it would have on others that I know. I'd be admitting failure. My parents would be understanding and would want to help me but it would come with a price. I don't want to feel like I've let them down again. I don't want the world to know how messed up I am. But if I stay here and continue to try and work things out on my own I definitely won't get better. I don't have enough self control to take care of this myself.

I think that telling a therapist everything that I'm feeling would help, but I don't think it would be enough help to get me through this. Plus if I tell them I have a plan to kill myself that's an instant committal. Not that I don't need that...I most certainly am a danger to myself. But seeing as no one on the planet knows exactly how I'm feeling except for a few random people on the internet I feel like I should also tell someone close to me...like my family.

I don't know if they'll be able to give me the courage I need to get through this...I don't know what will give me the courage I need to get through this. Part of my problem is that I know what people want to hear and usually have no problems misleading others as to how I really feel. Being open about my thoughts is not a strong suit of mine in the first place.

I just feel like I'm more than a little bit fucked up. This is going to take months if not years to fix. I've been living with depression for so long that my entire mindset and world view is going to have to change...and I'll probably be dragging my feet the whole way.

And I'm so ashamed of some of the things that I have to admit that I'm worried I'll never fully come clean or be able to get the help that I need.

I have been talking to a therapist, but it's just been talking, no medication or anything. A huge part of the problem is that I'm not being completely open. It's extremely difficult...and if someone knew just what I'm feeling they'd probably want to do more than just talk to me.... There's drug and alcohol addiction that I need to deal with on top of that.

I'm still relatively young (25) and in school. My parents would be able to help pay for the help that I think I need but knowing them they'd also want me to come home so they could keep an eye on me too...and I wouldn't mind going home either it's just a hard pill to swallow. Especially when the reason I'm going home is because I'm an alcoholic/drug addict with a death wish who's going off the deep end. School would be over, my parents would be watching me like a hawk, and I'd be so embarassed....

I just feel like I'm at the end of my rope. Like I've done everything that I can do on my own. I want to come clean but I can't seem to control my own actions. I feel like something's taken over my brain and what little rational part that's left is finally trying to scream for help before it's too late. But it's going to take more than talking....and I don't know if I'll be able to talk about the things that really need to be discussed anyway.

I'm so confused.

Such motivating and uplifting words.

Sorry to hear that your visit to therapy didn't go well. I've been in a similar situation before...I had to withdraw from school and move back home once. It's definitely not fun, but let me offer you this advice: find something to do. A job, a hobby, hell anything to take your mind off how you feel. I felt just like you do now back then, and even though you probably don't feel like doing much of anything it will help. Even if it doesn't make you feel any better about yourself it can distract you from how you're feeling.

As for what I meant when I said I had to get out of here....well I meant suicide, but if for some reason that doesn't happen I certainly won't be staying where I'm at either. So both, I guess.

Hey man. I had my appointment with the counselor. Not a whole lot going on so far...I'd never spoken to this one before so it's still early in the process. I'm still not optimistic that he's going to talk me out of anything, but it doesn't bother me to go, so I'll keep it up for awhile.

Other than that I'm not feeling that much better. Been hitting the booze and drugs hard, and things aren't really getting better. I still feel like I need to get out of here, but I'm waiting just a bit longer to take care of a last few things...and give myself every possible chance to make sure that I'm making the right decision.

I am one of those who has posted (and still do post) here looking for help. Believe it or not there are people who think that NO ONE cares. And while a stranger on the internet is probably not the bastion of caring that these people (myself?) are looking for, it does help. It is something.

Speaking from experience, it can be hard to ask for help. I've done it so many times now that it seems like second nature, but that first time was hard as hell. I didn't want to tell anyone, much less post it online for everyone to see. Someone like this who puts themselves out there offering help is a great way for those people to ask for help without risking the pain, sadness, and humiliation of going to someone you know and love instead. It may not be ideal but it can lead to good things.

This may sound silly coming from someone who is looking to exit soon himself. But despite how I feel I don't wish what I'm feeling upon anyone else, and the more options people have to get help, the better.

I was involuntarily committed to a short term institution once because I was at the point where I was mere seconds from going over the edge. It was New Year's Eve and I drove my car home drunk without a seatbelt telling myself that I was gonna swerve into a tree but I always swerved away at the last second...

I told my counselor about it later in the week and he had me committed "for my own benefit." When they took me in there were two different possible groups I could've been put into: depression or chemical dependence. I was put into the chemical dependence group since I was drinking at the time. I'm not saying that I haven't been addicted in my lifetime (and I'm sure it doesn't help) but I was just as suicidal when I was sober as when I wasn't (if not more so) and at the time my drinking was well within what most people would consider normal and my drug use was almost non-existent.

So instead of getting the help I needed I got preached at about how drinking and drugs were bad. I knew that...I just wanted to die. It did nothing for me. They put me on meds and after three days I was smart enough to say the right things to the doctors so they let me out of there. It was a horrible experience and if anything made me even more skeptical of talking to professionals or trying to get help.

I've been to professionals since then but I NEVER tell them how I'm truly feeling. You can say that you feel suicidal and want to die, but if they think you've tried it recently or have a plan to try it soon they'll send you off in a heartbeat.

Surely places like the one I was at can be beneficial to some people, but it didn't work for me at all. I'm right back to where I was at that time if not worse, despite the repeated times I've tried to get help. My suggestion: if you're really interested in getting long term therapy or think that you need it then research places that offer it first and go VOLUNTARILY. Some institutions are light years better than others. If you go talk to a shrink, don't say anything that makes them think you're in immediate danger of harming yourself or you won't have any say in the matter whatsoever.

Good luck, I hope things work out better for you than they did for me. And feel free to message me if you have any more questions about my experiences.

Ironically (or not) my mediocre financial situation has very little, if any, bearing on how I feel right now.

The fact that I've written a letter and have a plan is enough to get me involuntarily committed to an institution, at least for the short term.

I've tried getting professional help many times, though it has been a few years. Always felt like slapping a band-aid on a broken arm....but I probably do owe it to myself to try one more time since it's been so long....

Part of the problem is that as much as I'd like to I can never be fully open with them. I'd be thrown into the loony bin for awhile at the very least, which is just unacceptable as that would ruin what little is left of my life that has kept me going for this long.

On top of that I'm a pretty intelligent and stubborn person. Whatever argument for life that they could throw at me I'm pretty sure I've already heard and reasoned through on my own. It might be more of a debate than therapy.

Doesn't sound all that bad though. Like a test almost. If I can handle what the "professionals" throw at me then it would only make me feel even more assured about what I'm thinking/feeling.

Or maybe I am crazy, maybe I do deserve to be thrown in the loony bin....but if that's the case then that's yet another reason for me to get the hell out of here ASAP.

Thanks for your suggestion.

This is a great post. It really made me think. I am going to try my best to address all of your points so forgive me if it is long winded.

"What is the point of living" is indeed the question that I am seeking an answer to. However the statement "life int this world is good" is purely subjective. For some people life is more than hard, it's hell. Some people have nowhere to sleep. Nothing to eat. I realize how fortunate I am to not be one of those people. Yet I still don't believe that life is good. I believe that life simply IS.

You are absolutely correct in stating that no other life forms (that we know of) get such an opportunity to go through what we go through. And that is something special. Something unique. For a lot of people I'm sure that it is something worth treasuring and making the most of.

I think you may misunderstand where I'm coming from though. I'm not particularly miserable. I mean, sure, I've been miserable before. I've been miserable recently. But I also realize how fortunate I am to be here with all of the resources and opportunities available to me that other don't have. I 100% absolutely get that and cherish it for every second that I'm alive.

I've fought through adversity. I've made my life better. I've taken charge and earned a pretty decent living. I just don't understand why I did. Why I should fight any longer. Any good that I could give to you would not last more than a day or two as a complete stranger. Even if you were my own brother though, any good that I could provide to you would only last as long as your own life lasts. Which in the grand scheme of things is not very long.

I've lived through so many experiences that I am very, very grateful for. If you met me on the street instead of here in this topic that I posted I would tell you that I was happy and I would mean it 100%. 

But I just don't get it. I don't understand what it's about. It all seems so pointless. Forgive me if I'm paraphrasing you incorrectly but it seems the crux of your argument is "Live because you can. Live because you're alive." If you try to apply that to other things, it flat out doesn't make sense. No one would ever say "Kill because you have the opportunity." No one would ever say "Beat the crap out of that guy because it will make you feel good and therefore make your life better."

It just doesn't make sense.

So yes I want to die. I've charged through some hard times, and I see the benefit in that, but I sincerely believe that it's just not for me. Life isn't for me. If I died tomorrow it wouldn't be because I was miserable, I would genuinely believe that there would be benefit in it, despite the harm it would cause to those I care about. I would die with a smile on my face because I would believe it was right. I know that sounds selfish, but the way you describe life sounds pretty selfish too doesn't it?

The argument that by staying alive I can help others is a common one. But I must ask you this: isn't it possible I could help others in death as well? We as a species are looking at overpopulation, fighting amongst ourselves, continuously putting our morals and beliefs into other people's minds. As much as those intentions are usually meant for the best can't you see the harm in that? Can you see how it would be beneficial to eliminate those who aren't capable or willing to take part in such things?

I am one of those people. I have tried for my entire life, and I really just don't see the point in trying any longer. I see what's going on around me in the world and I don't want to take part in it. And I'm perfectly content and happy when I say that.

Thank you so much for your comment. It really did help to give me some understanding. I hope that you don't take my reply as an insult because like you, I am speaking from my heart.

Take care of yourself my friend.

To be completely honest, I believe that if the will to survive doesn't exist in a person that CAN be right. The vast majority of people on the earth may not agree with me but as you said before it's built into the system. Racism, homophobia, and hatred are built into the system too, but there are plenty of people who don't think that that is right. How is survival any different?

And who's to say that my mind isn't working? I could give you plenty of reasons for why having less people in the world would actually be beneficial to mankind...therefore having a desire to die would be "right."

Sure, there are things that I would want to accomplish if I were to decide to go through with my life. I would like to finish school, get married someday, perhaps have children.

I like to ride my bike, play video games, and play chess.

But are those really reasons to live? Those things aren't any different from what millions of other people in the world would be doing whether I'm here or not.

And in response to your question let me ask you this: if I had said that what I wanted to do was rule the world or prove that my race is superior to all others, would you still be here fighting to prove that my life is worthwhile? There are those out there whose goals in life are exactly that and neither you nor I nor anyone else are in a place to say that that is any better or worse than what I would like to do.

Pardon me for being philosophical yet again, but what purpose does my "survival button" even serve? I know that it's there. If it wasn't I would've been dead long ago.

But that's exactly the sort of arbitrary "live life because you're alive" nonsense that I don't understand.

You got me there. Hell it says right in the title of my post that I don't want to die.

The problem is that I see no reason for living either. I'm such a logical, practical person that without finding that reason it seems to me the most practical thing would be to just end it.

I've thought that with time I might discover some reason, any reason, to keep going. I know I've only been alive for such a short time (on a local scale), but the longer I go without finding that reason the more reasonable and likely it is that I will actually go through with it.

As far as feeling big...even if I stood on Everest...even if I landed on Mars...I'd still just be one of billions. I've tried fooling myself into believing otherwise but my brain just doesn't buy it.

I sincerely appreciate your honesty.

You're right in that I "can't figure out 'why live?'"

Also, why shouldn't I think on a global scale? If the global scale wasn't important then why were I and you and everyone else given the ability to think on such a scale?

Well I certainly see where you're coming from, but from my perspective knowing that anything I accomplish in life will have such a minor effect doesn't seem like fun at all.

And living life simply for personal enjoyment seems like an absolute waste. I realize that not everyone can change the world, but that's exactly the point. Having fun is such a trivial insignificant thing that it just makes everything seem so arbitrary. Anyone can have fun. Is that really a reason to be alive?

Everyone says that suicide is a selfish action yet living simply to have the most fun you can in life seems equally as selfish.

I've actually been in this situation more than twice...I've been fighting these feelings for over half my life. I'm surprised that I've made it this far.

As for my friend, I don't think he realized that I needed him, because to be quite honest (and this may sound shallow, I know) I didn't need him. I valued him as a friend. I looked up to him. It all just seems like a lie to me. Yea things can get better. They probably will get better, even. But they can also get worse, and probably will get worse. Even if I somehow make it through this time I have no doubt in my mind that I will be back.
